acceptance: The exact implementation changes only fuzz/Cargo.toml, fuzz/Cargo.lock, fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml, fuzz/README.md, fuzz/THIRD_PARTY.md, fuzz/.gitignore, fuzz/fuzz_targets/durable_id.rs, fuzz/fuzz_targets/bounded_utf8.rs, fuzz/fuzz_targets/bounded_vec.rs, and .github/workflows/fuzz-smoke.yml.
The root Cargo.toml, root Cargo.lock, every crates/morize-core production source file, public API, and the existing .github/workflows/ci.yml remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
fuzz/Cargo.toml is an independent nested workspace, publish=false, depends on morize-core only by local path, pins libfuzzer-sys exactly to 0.4.13, and adds no dependency to the root workspace graph.
fuzz/Cargo.lock is committed and cargo metadata --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --locked succeeds; the root Cargo.lock remains unchanged.
fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml pins nightly-2026-09-18 with a minimal profile, and the fuzz workflow verifies the resolved rustc toolchain before running targets.

The fuzz workflow downloads cargo-fuzz exactly at version 0.13.2, verifies the pinned Linux x86_64 musl release asset SHA-256 b5b704018b63e0f151c17a057ac53b5111e1db545d1b9f72fee79f08a545931c, treats that musl artifact only as the cargo-fuzz executable, and explicitly builds/runs fuzz targets for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu so AddressSanitizer is not combined with statically linked musl libc.

fuzz/THIRD_PARTY.md records cargo-fuzz as MIT OR Apache-2.0 and libfuzzer-sys 0.4.13 as (MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND NCSA, states that bundled libFuzzer sources carry NCSA, and confines all such code/dependencies to fuzz-only verification.

durable_id fuzz target consumes arbitrary raw bytes without unsafe code; whenever an input is valid UTF-8 and a durable-ID parser succeeds, the result must round-trip through canonical lowercase text and exact bytes for every durable identifier type without panic.

bounded_utf8 fuzz target consumes arbitrary raw bytes, considers only valid UTF-8, exercises multiple fixed const byte limits, and asserts acceptance iff encoded length is within the limit, exact byte preservation on success, and exact TooLong metadata on rejection.

bounded_vec fuzz target consumes arbitrary raw bytes, exercises multiple fixed const item limits, and asserts exact construction/push acceptance, preserved order/values, lossless rejected-value recovery, and no mutation after rejected push.

All fuzz targets are pure invariant harnesses: they perform no network, filesystem fixture, environment-variable, wall-clock, model, persistence, serialization, or mutation-authority operation and introduce no unsafe block in Morize-authored target code.
A dedicated fuzz-smoke workflow runs only on Ubuntu/Linux, leaves the existing Ubuntu/macOS/Windows product CI unchanged, and never makes Windows support depend on libFuzzer.

The fuzz-smoke workflow explicitly uses target triple x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and bounds each target with fixed run count, input-size limit, timeout, RSS ceiling, and explicit seed while still executing coverage-guided libFuzzer rather than deterministic property loops.

The fuzz-smoke workflow runs all three targets and fails on any crash, sanitizer finding, timeout/crash artifact, assertion failure, build failure, lock drift, toolchain/version mismatch, or dependency/license-isolation violation.
On fuzz failure, the workflow uploads fuzz crash/artifact output using a commit-pinned artifact action; absence of a crash artifact on success is not treated as missing evidence.
The fuzz workspace and smoke workflow do not claim exhaustive fuzzing, bug absence, coverage completeness, or security proof; bounded smoke evidence is explicitly scoped to the executed run budget.

cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline continue to pass for the root workspace.
The dedicated fuzz workspace builds all three fuzz targets with the pinned nightly/tool/dependency graph and completes the bounded fuzz-smoke campaign on Linux.
The standard GitHub Actions matrix continues to pass Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows on the exact implementation head, and the dedicated Linux fuzz-smoke workflow passes on that same implementation head.

Before WorkPacket export, the canonical repository Diffcipline policy admits exactly the new `fuzz/**` expected-file surface required by this Grain, while preserving the existing forbidden surfaces, verification commands, dependency-manifest policy, lockfile policy, and untracked-file policy unchanged.

Diffcipline verifies the exact implementation head with no scope violation; Alibaba Open Code Review accounts for every changed file; an independent semantic reviewer separately reviews isolation, target invariants, toolchain/tool identity, bounded campaign semantics, license closure, failure-artifact behavior, and non-claims.
ADR-0004 proof prerequisites SG-000012, SG-000013, SG-000014, and SG-000023 revalidate against the exact WorkPacket baseline before execution.

method.control: Implementation is limited to an isolated fuzz workspace, three raw-byte fuzz targets, fuzz-only license/provenance documentation, and one Linux-only bounded fuzz-smoke workflow. The root Cargo workspace, root Cargo.lock, morize-core production source, public APIs, standard cross-platform CI, runtime behavior, persistence, serialization, and domain semantics must remain unchanged. Before WorkPacket export, the canonical planning baseline must admit only `fuzz/**` to Diffcipline `expected_files`; that baseline governance correction is not part of the ten-file implementation diff and must not weaken any other Diffcipline policy field.
method.review_separation: An independent semantic reviewer must review the exact implementation head for isolation from the root workspace/runtime graph, target invariant fidelity, bounded true-libFuzzer execution, pinned toolchain/tool identity, license handling, failure artifact behavior, scope containment, and required evidence separately from the implementing agent before acceptance.
method.rollback: Revert the SG-000024 fuzz workspace/workflow commit. Root runtime code, root lockfile, persisted data, public APIs, and user data are unaffected.

minimality.rationale: An independent fuzz workspace with raw-byte targets and one Linux-only smoke lane is the narrowest true-libFuzzer increment that satisfies the remaining P1 fuzz requirement without adding any root/runtime dependency or changing product CI portability.

requirements: Fuzz tooling and its NCSA component must remain dev/fuzz-only and must not link into Morize runtime artifacts.

The bounded CI campaign must fail closed on crashes, assertions, sanitizer findings, tool/version drift, lock drift, or isolation violations, while avoiding claims of exhaustive fuzzing or bug absence.
Crash inputs may contain arbitrary generated bytes and must not include real user data, secrets, PHI, repository credentials, or copied production fixtures.

outcome: Morize has an isolated, reproducible, zero-runtime-impact libFuzzer harness for the durable-ID parser and bounded UTF-8/ordered-collection primitives, with pinned fuzz tooling, bounded Linux smoke execution, independent fuzz-only dependency/license closure, and no coupling to the root workspace or production artifacts.
rationale: P1 explicitly requires property and fuzz tests for parsers/invariants. SG-000023 closed the deterministic property-matrix portion while explicitly deferring a true fuzz campaign. The official rust-fuzz cargo-fuzz/libfuzzer-sys path provides coverage-guided libFuzzer execution but requires nightly and sanitizer support and is not a Windows production concern, so the smallest safe next slice is an isolated fuzz workspace plus a Linux-only bounded smoke gate. The published cargo-fuzz Linux binary used by CI is musl-linked, so the workflow must distinguish tool artifact identity from fuzz target identity and pass --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu to avoid AddressSanitizer/static-libc incompatibility.

risk.recovery: Revert the isolated fuzz workspace/workflow implementation. Root runtime code, standard product CI contract, root lockfile, persisted data, public APIs, and user data are unaffected.

scope_in: Create an independent fuzz Cargo workspace rooted at fuzz/ with its own lockfile and toolchain pin; keep it outside the root workspace graph without modifying root Cargo.toml or root Cargo.lock.

Pin libfuzzer-sys exactly to 0.4.13 and cargo-fuzz exactly to 0.13.2; verify the published Linux x86_64 musl cargo-fuzz executable checksum before use, and explicitly compile/run fuzz targets for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.
Implement three raw-byte libFuzzer targets covering durable-ID parser canonicalization, BoundedUtf8 byte-bound invariants, and BoundedVec item-bound/lossless-rejection invariants.
Add one Ubuntu-only fuzz-smoke workflow that executes bounded coverage-guided runs for every target and uploads crash artifacts on failure.
Document fuzz-only dependency licensing/provenance, local reproduction commands, bounded-smoke semantics, and explicit non-claims.

Admit only `fuzz/**` to the canonical repository Diffcipline `expected_files` policy before WorkPacket export so the authorized isolated fuzz workspace can be proved without weakening forbidden surfaces, verification commands, dependency/lock policy, or untracked-file handling.
scope_out: Any root Cargo workspace member/exclude change, root Cargo.lock change, morize-core production source/public API change, runtime dependency, build dependency, production packaging linkage, or user-facing runtime behavior.
Windows libFuzzer support, replacing the existing cross-platform product CI, making product correctness depend on fuzz infrastructure, or requiring nightly for normal Morize builds.

Long-running scheduled campaigns, distributed fuzzing, OSS-Fuzz enrollment, persistent corpus governance, coverage thresholds, mutation dictionaries, custom mutators, structure-aware Arbitrary inputs, Miri, sanitizers beyond cargo-fuzz defaults, or fuzzing later persistence/network/policy layers.
Any claim of exhaustive fuzzing, proof of bug absence, complete security coverage, or completion of future fuzz targets outside the three authorized P1 primitives.
title: Add isolated true-fuzz harness for core invariants
